name: AL-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Terri Sewell holds a $3.75M-to-$116K cash advantage over challenger Ammie Akin
District leans Democratic by about ten points and has delivered landslides for Sewell
Prediction markets price Sewell near 98 percent to win
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race
model.rationale: Sewell combines incumbency, a D+10 district, and a roughly 25-to-1 fundraising edge over a first-time challenger, while markets price her near 98 percent; nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: An unexpected scandal or a late wave of outside spending against Sewell could narrow the margin, though an upset remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Terri Sewell seeks another term in Alabama's 7th District, a Birmingham-to-Black Belt seat that leans Democratic by about ten points on the partisan index. She faces Republican Ammie Akin, a first-time challenger with minimal financial backing. Sewell has raised nearly $2 million and holds $3.75 million on hand, dwarfing Akin's $150,000 raised and $116,000 in cash. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets price Sewell's chances near 98 percent.

The district's composition, anchored by Birmingham and much of the Black Belt, has produced wide margins for Sewell in past cycles, and the national House environment adds a modest Democratic tilt this year. With an entrenched incumbent, an overwhelming money advantage, and no visible signs of a competitive challenge, the seat sits firmly in the safe Democratic column.
